key_insight: A high-order multiscale method captures heterogeneous wave propagation with fractional history-dependent damping using homogenized dynamics and first- and second-order corrections.
engineering_relevance: The method reduces the computational burden of simulating waves in composite materials with rapidly varying, discontinuous properties.
method: Derive a homogenized wave equation and microscale corrections through multiscale asymptotic expansion.
Establish local balance preservation and global O(ε) energy-norm convergence.
Combine finite elements with an L2-1σ–Newmark time scheme and prove unconditional shifted-energy stability.
evidence_signal: Two- and three-dimensional numerical examples demonstrate accuracy, efficiency, reduced computational cost, and robustness, although the abstract reports no quantitative speedups.
watch_item: Implementation must account for fractional-history storage and computation, which the abstract does not quantify.
paper_title: A high-order multi-scale method and its error analysis for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems in composite materials
